correctness.rationale: Tree edge root generators b_e are linearly independent by leaf elimination, making its centered zonotope a linear image of the (n−1)-cube. The intrinsic facet dual normals for the two chosen cuts are u_e=1_A−(a/n)1 and u_f=1_C−(c/n)1 with A,C disjoint outer components of T minus two edges. Their normalized inner product is −sqrt(ac/((a+b)(b+c))). Each edge pair produces four parallelotope ridges with outward signs split evenly, giving two acute arccos(q) and two obtuse pi−arccos(q), count 2(n−1)(n−2), mean pi/2, never right. Maximizing q²=(a/(n−a))(c/(n−c)) under positive a,b,c yields b=1 and balanced a,c, iff a degree-two balanced vertex; q>=1/(n−1) universally with star iff all maximizing pairs give a=c=1. Tested independent exact cut normal q for path and star trees at n=3,4,5,10, reproducing equality extrema, plus fully inspected exact finite checker. Infinite result follows from algebra/graph structure, not sampled trees.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for all ridges of canonical tree graphical zonotopes and both sharp extremal tree equality characterizations. A same-date cycle-zonotope theorem uses the very same cut-size cosine q but only obtuse cycle ridges; it neither implies supplementary four-ridge multiplicities for tree parallelotopes nor the star/balanced-degree-two tree classification. The dual-normal computation is classical and not alone asserted original.
residual_risks: The cycle formula is a closely related same-date overlap, so exact publication order and whether a broader graph-theoretic angle theorem exists remain priority risks.
No classification for arbitrary positive edge weights or cyclic graphs is implied; unit-root intrinsic metric is essential.

value.rationale: A canonical tree zonotope is combinatorially a cube regardless of tree, but its Euclidean ridge angles retain cut-size information. The four-ridge decomposition and exact sharp extremizers identify geometric structure invisible to the common face lattice, a natural complete metric classification rather than an arbitrary angle table.

limitations: Only standard unit-root Euclidean tree embedding, no weighted edges/cyclic graphs; related same-day cycle angle theorem overlaps cosine expression.
